newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico PRI puts off decision on Carlos Salinas fate.
newsitem.headline: Mexico PRI puts off decision on Carlos Salinas fate.

text.p: The ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) postponed on Wednesday for a second time a controversial decision on whether to expel disgraced former President Carlos Salinas from the party.

PRI officials put off ruling on the proposal by rank-and-file members until after key mid-term elections in July, in which President Ernesto Zedillo's party faces tough competition from the opposition.

"We decided to resolve this issue after the elections on July 6...we did not want people thinking we did this for electoral purposes," Vicente Fuentes, head of the PRI's Honor and Justice Commission, told reporters.

Carlos Salinas, who now lives in self-imposed exile in Ireland, won huge acclaim during his 1988-94 administration but fell into disgrace soon afterward as the economy collapsed and accusations mounted of corruption during his term.

Carlos's brother Raul -- imprisoned since 1995 on murder and illicit enrichment charges -- was kicked out of the party in January 1996 and calls from party faithful have since grown louder for the former president to face a similar fate.
Political analysts say expelling Salinas from the party would win votes for the PRI, which has ruled Mexico for 68 years but has witnessed its worst electoral defeats to date in the past two years.

PRI president Humberto Roque Villanueva told Reuters in a recent interview the party would expel Salinas if it were proven he had broken the law. Roque said he had yet to see conclusive evidence that this was the case.

But the PRI leader said on Friday his party was "politically and morally distanced" from Salinas and accused the former president of being ideologically closer to the conservative opposition party PAN than to the PRI.
The issue of whether or not to expell Salinas from the PRI underscores simmering divisions within the party, political analysts say.
Some party hardliners want to repudiate Salinas' entire legacy, including his economic reforms, and those who worked closely with the former leader who are still in power.

"Distancing oneself from Carlos Salinas de Gortari implies separating oneself from his policies and not just making declarations because "Salinismo" (the Salinas style) is still alive and kicking in the policy of Ernesto Zedillo", said the left-wing National Democratic Alliance in a statement.
President Zedillo was a cabinet member during the Salinas administration and, while personally distant now from Salinas, has closely followed his predecessor's economic liberalization policies.
